paper.title_en: Simplifying 2-Bundle Descriptions of Invariants and Local Dynamics
paper.abstract_en: A string couples to a 2-form gauge potential whose local descriptions need not fit together as a single global form. Principal 2-bundles provide a geometric description of this gluing. However, we recover surface amplitudes and quantum partition functions, as well as local classical field dynamics, without the 2-bundle formalism. For surface amplitudes, differential characters preserve curvature and flat phases. Ordinary fake-flat crossed-module connections with a fixed flat quotient and a reference lift lead to abelian differential cocycles with local coefficients. In three-dimensional finite gauge theories with cohomological actions, Fourier transformation evaluates the 2-form field sum and gives a sum of ordinary finite-group gauge partition functions. A four-dimensional quadratic example gives a signature response that admits direct cochain evaluation although replacement by an ordinary finite-group gauge theory fails. Established bundle, operator, and module descriptions provide further comparisons for topological and index invariants and twisted-sheaf moduli. For finite-dimensional smoothly separable central crossed modules, an invertible local substitution removes a pure gauge 1-form from invariant classical actions for any adjustment, leaving an ordinary quotient connection and two tensor fields. One of these tensor fields can be separated globally from the remaining lift data after fixing the quotient connection and choosing a smooth bundle splitting. For compact or semisimple quotients, an equivariant splitting makes this separation compatible with the full gauge symmetry without changing the adjustment.
